newsitem.title: USA: U.S. ports fear loss of funding after court ruling.
newsitem.headline: U.S. ports fear loss of funding after court ruling.

text.p: A U.S. court decision against a key federal harbor tax has put funding for shipping channel maintenance in jeopardy, a U.S. ports group said on Wednesday.
The U.S. Court of Appeals on Tuesday ruled that the U.S. harbor maintenance tax, which levies a 12.5 cent fee on every $100 of cargo value, is unconstitutional.

"...(T)his decision could have serious economic implications for the country and its ability to compete in the international marketplace," American Association of Port Authorities (AAPA) President Kurt Nagle said in a statement.
"It is essential that there be continued funding to maintain navigation channels to ports and to ensure the flow of commerce," he added.

Enacted in 1986 to fund maintenance dredging of federal navigation channels, the tax was tripled to its current level in 1990. The Court of Appeals decision affirmed a lower court ruling made in October 1995.
Nearly $700 million in fees was collected and deposited in the Harbor Maintenance Trust Fund in fiscal 1995, the most recent year for which figures are available.
Exporters have argued the tax imposes an unfair burden on them and the federal government should bear a larger share of maintenance costs.
Both shippers and port officials said they expected the decision would be appealed to the U.S. Supreme Court.
((-- W Pollack, New York Commodities Desk +1 212 859 1640))
